The map from the Bass–Serre tree of ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ to the tree is locally injective, hence injective, so the group is ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ = ⟨g₁, g₂ | g₁²⟩ with finite vertex stabilizers: discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 2/3 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.73227953π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: Bass–Serre on the pair g₂·g₂·g₂·g₁, g₂: the bridge between the cores of g₂·g₂·g₂·g₁ and g₂ has length 0, and each finite factor moves its end of the bridge freely. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: |tr²g2 − 4| + |tr[g2, g1·g2·g1] − 2| ≈ 0.98093635 < 1. ⟨g2, g1·g2·g1⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g2, g1·g2·g1] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g2, g1·g2·g1⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point (the value evaluated with 256 bits).

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: |tr²g2 − 4| + |tr[g2, g1·g2·g1] − 2| ≈ 0.9411255 < 1. ⟨g2, g1·g2·g1⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g2, g1·g2·g1] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g2, g1·g2·g1⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has (g1²·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1²·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2·g1·g2 fixes the fixed point of the parabolic g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2·g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹·g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹·g2⁻¹ and multiplies its translation by μ ≈ 0.41421356, |μ| ≈ 0.41421356 ≠ 1. The common fixed point and μ are exact (g·N·g⁻¹ = μ·N over K, for the nilpotent part N of the parabolic), and so are μ⁴ ≠ 1 and μ⁶ ≠ 1. The parabolics (g2·g1·g2)ⁿ·(g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2·g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹·g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹·g2⁻¹)·(g2·g1·g2)⁻ⁿ translate by μⁿτ, which shrinks to 0 as n → +∞: non-trivial elements converging to the identity, so the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

The map from the Bass–Serre tree of ℤ ∗ ℤ/2 to the tree is locally injective, hence injective, so the group is ℤ ∗ ℤ/2 = ⟨g₁, g₂ | g₂²⟩ with finite vertex stabilizers: discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 3/4 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.71490104π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det ≈ 1.1708204 (a root of x² − x − 1/5) is real (numerically: |Im| < 10⁻¹⁰) and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.63607493π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/3 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.60817345π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete

The parabolics (g1²·g2⁻²)ⁿ·(g1·g2²)·(g1²·g2⁻²)⁻ⁿ translate by μⁿτ, which shrinks to 0 as n → +∞: non-trivial elements converging to the identity, so the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1²·g2⁻² is elliptic: tr²/det = 1/16 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.92021382π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has (g1²·g2⁻²)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1²·g2⁻² has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det ≈ 1.7320508 (a root of x² − 3) is real (numerically: |Im| < 10⁻¹⁰) and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.54277406π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 fixes the fixed point of the parabolic g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 and multiplies its translation by μ ≈ 1.7320508, |μ| ≈ 1.7320508 ≠ 1. places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ is elliptic: tr²/det = 49/16 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.32172249π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has (g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: |tr²g2 − 4| + |tr[g2, g1·g2] − 2| ≈ 0.17163337 < 1. ⟨g2, g1·g2⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g2, g1·g2] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g2, g1·g2⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ
places.detail: Bass–Serre: g₁ fixes one point of the axis of g₂ and moves both axis directions there freely and off each other. The map from the Bass–Serre tree of ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ to the tree is locally injective, hence injective, so the group is ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ = ⟨g₁, g₂ | g₁²⟩ with finite vertex stabilizers: discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det ≈ 2.604339 (a root of x² − 40/13x + 16/13) is real (numerically: |Im| < 10⁻¹⁰) and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.40228915π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 4; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: g2 fixes the fixed point of the parabolic g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 and multiplies its translation by μ ≈ 0.8660254, |μ| ≈ 0.8660254 ≠ 1. The common fixed point and μ are exact (g·N·g⁻¹ = μ·N over K, for the nilpotent part N of the parabolic), and so are μ⁴ ≠ 1 and μ⁶ ≠ 1. The parabolics g2ⁿ·(g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)·g2⁻ⁿ translate by μⁿτ, which shrinks to 0 as n → +∞: non-trivial elements converging to the identity, so the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/3
places.detail: Bass–Serre on the pair g₁, g₁·g₂: the bridge between the cores of g₁ and g₁·g₂ has length 0, and each finite factor moves its end of the bridge freely. places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ is elliptic: tr²/det ≈ 0.62996052 (a root of x³ − 1/4) is real (numerically: |Im| < 10⁻¹⁰) and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.74020644π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 6; no such m has (g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1 fixes the fixed point of the parabolic g1·g2·g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹·g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹·g2·g1⁻¹·g2⁻¹ and multiplies its translation by μ ≈ -0.62996052 + 1.0911236i, |μ| ≈ 1.259921 ≠ 1. The common fixed point and μ are exact (g·N·g⁻¹ = μ·N over K, for the nilpotent part N of the parabolic), and so are μ⁴ ≠ 1 and μ⁶ ≠ 1. The parabolics (g1·g2·g1)ⁿ·(g1·g2·g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹·g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹·g2·g1⁻¹·g2⁻¹)·(g1·g2·g1)⁻ⁿ translate by μⁿτ, which shrinks to 0 as n → −∞: non-trivial elements converging to the identity, so the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det ≈ 2.0268108 (a root of x³ − 3x² + 9/4x − 9/16) is real (numerically: |Im| < 10⁻¹⁰) and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.4957328π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 6; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: |tr²g1³ − 4| + |tr[g1³, g2³] − 2| ≈ 0.94450731 < 1. ⟨g1³, g2³⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g1³, g2³] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g1²·g2⁻¹, g1·g2·g1⁻¹⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1²·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det ≈ 3.5980409 (a root of x³ − 27/4x² + 117/8x − 3025/256) is real (numerically: |Im| < 10⁻¹⁰) and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.20535186π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 6; no such m has (g1²·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1²·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 6; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

The common fixed point and μ are exact (g·N·g⁻¹ = μ·N over K, for the nilpotent part N of the parabolic), and so are μ⁴ ≠ 1 and μ⁶ ≠ 1. The parabolics g2ⁿ·(g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)·g2⁻ⁿ translate by μⁿτ, which shrinks to 0 as n → −∞: non-trivial elements converging to the identity, so the group is not discrete.

places.detail: The group fixes a point but is infinite: g₁ is elliptic of infinite order, so the group lies in a compact stabilizer without being finite.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det ≈ 2.324718 (a root of x³ − 3x² + 2x − 1) is real (numerically: |Im| < 10⁻¹⁰) and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.44808974π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 6; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 fixes the fixed point of the parabolic g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 and multiplies its translation by μ ≈ 0.78492015 − 1.3071413i, |μ| ≈ 1.5247026 ≠ 1. The common fixed point and μ are exact (g·N·g⁻¹ = μ·N over K, for the nilpotent part N of the parabolic), and so are μ⁴ ≠ 1 and μ⁶ ≠ 1. The parabolics g2ⁿ·(g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)·g2⁻ⁿ translate by μⁿτ, which shrinks to 0 as n → −∞: non-trivial elements converging to the identity, so the group is not discrete.
